data.body:
rebar-debug Phase 1 (reproduce-before-repair) on current origin/main (234a07b55) — scope narrowed by evidence:

REPRODUCED the original symptom faithfully: real rebar store on a bare origin, then a 'git clone --single-branch --branch main' (no refs/remotes/origin/tickets), then 'rebar init --silent'. RESULT: the clone now ADOPTS origin/tickets (rebar list returns the existing ticket; tracker root sha == origin root sha; merge-base clean). So AC1 no longer reproduces — the landed sync refspec fixes (5546/35f7) self-heal it: sync fetches via the explicit '+refs/heads/tickets:refs/remotes/origin/tickets' refspec (sync.py:234) and the empty-local unrelated-history arm union-adopts the shared tracker (sync.py:141-149).

Coverage already exists for AC1/AC4 and the sync side of AC2 in tests/unit/test_sync_narrow_refspec.py: test_empty_orphan_store_adopts_shared_tracker_under_narrow_refspec (AC1/AC4) and test_orphan_store_with_events_is_refused_and_reported_diverged (AC2: a non-empty orphan is refused and a DIVERGED warning is LOGGED by sync).

REMAINING REAL GAP = AC3. The DIVERGED condition sync detects is only emitted as a best-effort log line during implicit sync. The dedicated health check, 'rebar fsck', does NOT surface it: fsck._push_pending (fsck.py:363-392) runs 'rev-list remote_ref..HEAD --count' with no merge-base check, so a genuinely divergent store is mislabeled 'PUSH_PENDING: ... ahead of origin/tickets by N — push pending' (informational, exit 0) — or 'no issues found' when the tracking ref is absent. Reproduced: a tracker with no common ancestor to origin/tickets (merge-base exit 1) => fsck prints PUSH_PENDING and does not count it as an issue.

FIX (this ticket): teach fsck to distinguish DIVERGED (no common ancestor, or common-ancestor-but-non-fast-forwardable) from PUSH_PENDING (remote is an ancestor of HEAD), mirroring the taxonomy in _store/sync.py, and report DIVERGED as a COUNTED issue (non-zero exit) naming the recovery path. This delivers AC3 and satisfies AC2's 'no silent data-hiding' intent via the health check. No init.py rearchitecture is needed (would be redundant with the landed self-heal and adds risk in a 692-LOC file). Out of scope, unchanged: the init-time ls-remote probe / loud-fail-at-init proposal from the earlier root-cause comment is superseded by the landed self-heal + this fsck detection.
